source_text:
Ταύτῃ οὖν τῇ ἐλπίδι προσδεδέσθωσαν αἱ ψυχαὶ ἡμῶν τῷ πιστῷ ἐν ταῖς ἐπαγγελίαις καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐν τοῖς κρίμασιν.
ὁ παραγγείλας μὴ ψεύδεσθαι, πολλῷ μᾶλλον αὐτὸς οὐ ψεύσεται: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἀδύνατον παρὰ τῷ θεῷ εἰ μὴ τὸ ψεύσασθαι.
ἀναζωπυρησάτω οὖν ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ νοήσωμεν ὅτι πάντα ἐγγὺς αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
ἐν λόγῳ τῆς μεγαλωσύνης αὐτοῦ συνεστήσατο τὰ πάντα, καὶ ἐν λόγῳ δύναται αὐτὰ καταστρέψαι.
Τίς ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ: Τί ἐποίησας; ἢ τίς ἀντιστήσεται τῷ κράτει τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ; ὅτε θέλει καὶ ὡς θέλει ποιήσει πάντα, καὶ οὐδὲν μὴ παρέλθῃ τῶν δεδογματισμένων ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.
πάντα ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ εἰσίν, καὶ οὐδὲν λέληθεν τὴν βουλὴν αὐτοῦ,
εἰ οἱ οὐρανοὶ διηγοῦνται δόξαν θεοῦ, ποίησιν δὲ χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ἀναγγέλλει τὸ στερέωμα: ἡ ἡμέρα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐρεύγεται ῥῆμα, καὶ νὺξ νυκτὶ ἀναγγέλλει γνῶσιν: καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν λόγοι οὐδὲ λαλιαί, ὧν οὐχὶ ἀκούονται αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν.
thought_title: God's power and truthfulness ground our hope
orientation: The author has just cited Scripture about resurrection and now turns to God's faithfulness and power as the ground for hope.
pass_a_gloss: To this therefore hope let be bound the souls of us to the faithful [one] in the promises and to the just [one] in the judgments. The [one] having commanded not to lie, much more he himself will not lie; for nothing [is] impossible with God except the lying. Let be rekindled therefore the faith of him in us, and let us understand that all things near to him are. By word of the majesty of him he established all things, and by word he is able them to destroy. Who will say to him: What did you do? Or who will stand against the might of the strength of him? When he wishes and as he wishes he will do all things, and nothing shall pass away of the things decreed by him. All things before him are, and nothing has escaped the counsel of him, if the heavens declare glory of God, and [the] making of hands of him announces the firmament; the day to the day pours forth speech, and night to night announces knowledge; and there are not words nor speeches, of which not are heard the voices of them.

choices.why: The perfect passive imperative conveys a state of being fastened or attached; 'bound' keeps the physical metaphor of attachment to hope.
The verb means to stir up a fire again; 'rekindled' preserves the fire imagery and the passive imperative force.
The middle aorist of συνίστημι means to set together, constitute, or establish; 'established' fits the context of creation by God's word.
The verb means to overturn or bring down; 'destroy' captures the contrast with establishing all things.
The perfect participle of δογματίζω refers to things fixed by decree or decision; 'decreed' preserves the sense of divine ordinance.
The verb literally means to belch or gush out; 'pours forth' keeps the vivid image of day emitting speech while remaining idiomatic.

bible_refs.note: οἱ οὐρανοὶ διηγοῦνται δόξαν θεοῦ, ποίησιν δὲ χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ἀναγγέλλει τὸ στερέωμα: ἡ ἡμέρα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐρεύγεται ῥῆμα, καὶ νὺξ νυκτὶ ἀναγγέλλει γνῶσιν: καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν λόγοι οὐδὲ λαλιαί, ὧν οὐχὶ ἀκούονται αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν

pass_b_english: So let our souls be bound to this hope, to the one who is faithful in his promises and just in his judgments.
The one who commanded us not to lie will certainly not lie himself. For nothing is impossible with God except lying.
So let his faith be rekindled in us, and let us understand that all things are near to him.
By the word of his majesty he established all things, and by a word he can destroy them.

Who will say to him, “What have you done?” Or who will stand against the might of his strength? He will do all things when he wills and as he wills, and none of the things decreed by him will pass away.
All things are before him, and nothing has escaped his counsel.

The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands. Day pours forth speech to day, and night announces knowledge to night. There are no words or speeches whose voices are not heard (Psalm 19:1-4).

problems.source_quote: εἰ οἱ οὐρανοὶ διηγοῦνται δόξαν θεοῦ, ποίησιν δὲ χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ἀναγγέλλει τὸ στερέωμα: ἡ ἡμέρα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐρεύγεται ῥῆμα, καὶ νὺξ νυκτὶ ἀναγγέλλει γνῶσιν: καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν λόγοι οὐδὲ λαλιαί, ὧν οὐχὶ ἀκούονται αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν
problems.why: LXX Psalm 18 = English Psalm 19, but LXX Psalm 19 = English Psalm 20. The Greek matches LXX Psalm 18:1-4, so English should cite Psalm 19:1-4, not 19:1-3.
problems.ruling: Greek includes ὧν οὐχὶ ἀκούονται αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν = LXX Ps 18:4, so English should cite 19:1-4, not 19:1-3.

last_rejected.quote: So let his faith be rekindled in us
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀναζωπυρησάτω οὖν ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν
last_rejected.why: αὐτοῦ likely refers to God's faithfulness, not 'his faith' in us; ambiguous but potentially misleading.
last_rejected.fix: So let faith in him be rekindled in us
last_rejected.ruling: αὐτοῦ is genitive; 'his faith(fulness)' is normal range; 'faith be rekindled' captures sense.

last_rejected.quote: and none of the things decreed by him will pass away
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ οὐδὲν μὴ παρέλθῃ τῶν δεδογματισμένων ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: οὐδὲν μὴ παρέλθῃ = 'nothing will pass away/escape' but μὴ with subjunctive is emphatic negation 'will by no means.' However, 'will pass away' misses that παρέλθῃ here means 'pass by, go unnoticed, be annulled'—in context of decrees, 'fail' or 'be set aside.' 'Pass away' suggests temporal passing, not 'go unfulfilled.'
last_rejected.fix: and nothing decreed by him will fail
last_rejected.ruling: παρέλθῃ with decrees naturally means 'pass away/fail'; 'pass away' is within normal range here.

last_rejected.quote: For nothing is impossible with God except lying
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἀδύνατον παρὰ τῷ θεῷ εἰ μὴ τὸ ψεύσασθαι
last_rejected.why: εἰ μὴ here means 'except'—but this is a striking claim. 'Nothing is impossible with God except lying' makes lying the sole exception. This is theologically significant and accurately rendered. However, checking: is 'with God' correct for παρὰ τῷ θεῷ? Yes, 'with God' or 'for God.' Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms translation is correct; no actual error identified.

last_rejected.quote: and by a word he can destroy them
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ἐν λόγῳ δύναται αὐτὰ καταστρέψαι
last_rejected.why: ἐν λόγῳ = 'by a word' (instrumental). Correct. καταστρέψαι = 'overthrow, destroy, bring to an end.' 'Destroy' is strong but in range. However, 'destroy' suggests annihilation; 'bring to nothing' or 'overthrow' might be better. But 'destroy' is within semantic range. Not error.
last_rejected.ruling: καταστρέψαι includes 'destroy'; within normal semantic range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: Who will stand against the might of his strength
last_rejected.source_quote: ἢ τίς ἀντιστήσεται τῷ κράτει τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: κράτει τῆς ἰσχύος = 'might of his strength'—hendiadys-like. 'Might of his strength' is redundant but literal. 'The power of his might' is more natural. But 'might of his strength' is awkward English. Is it unreadable? Slightly awkward but comprehensible. Not major.
last_rejected.fix: who will withstand the power of his might
last_rejected.ruling: 'Might of his strength' is awkward but comprehensible; mere preference, not major error.

last_rejected.quote: nothing has escaped his counsel. The heavens declare the glory of God
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδὲν λέληθεν τὴν βουλὴν αὐτοῦ, εἰ οἱ οὐρανοὶ διηγοῦνται δόξαν θεοῦ
last_rejected.why: The source’s εἰ makes the psalm the ground of the claim; English states both as separate assertions.
last_rejected.fix: All things are before him, and nothing has escaped his counsel, since the heavens declare the glory of God
last_rejected.ruling: Source ends the clause with a comma and εἰ; it opens a new clause continuing into the psalm. Splitting into separate sentences is a defensible punctuation choice; meaning is basically preserved.

last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν λόγοι οὐδὲ λαλιαί, ὧν οὐχὶ ἀκούονται αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν.
last_rejected.why: The quotation ends at English Psalm 19:3. Verse 4, their voice going through the earth, is not quoted.
last_rejected.fix: There are no words or speeches whose voices are not heard (Psalm 19:1-3).
last_rejected.ruling: LXX Psalm 18:2-4 includes "οὐκ εἰσὶν λόγοι... αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν" (v.3 English), but LXX/Hebrew numbering; 1-4 range is a loose but acceptable citation, not misleading.
